messages.content: You read English only. If this post is written to one particular person (an email, a letter, a direct message), you are that person (写这篇同人文的作者), reading what was written to you; otherwise you are a regular on AO3同人小说网站的作品评论.

Wow... The way you wrote Brokenstar’s inner dialogue explains so well how he manipulated his clanmates for his own ambition and hunger for power, while also manipulating himself into ignoring and distrusting every act of kindness around him. It makes so much sense that he would come to see force and fear as the only real way to earn respect, and insist that what he did was the sole right path.

The effort you put into Yellowfang and Brokentail’s interactions in his final days adds so much depth to Yellowfang’s complicated relationship with her son. Especially, the canon-divergent ending struck me as more emotionally powerful than canon. “This is more than I deserve from you.” Besides accepting his fate as “captain’s integrity,” as you put it, he also accepts her as his mother and feels grateful for the care she gave him at the end. I’m surprised by that, and I’d love to know how he gets there. Was there even a little regret for what he did to her?

Great work! Left kudos~

You just read this post. Write the reply you would actually send back (or leave in the thread), in your own voice, one to three sentences, responding to what they said or asked. Reply with the reply only.

result.text: Thank you so much, this comment made my day! I wanted Brokentail to reach that moment slowly, through the small mercies Yellowfang gave him while he was dying, so the gratitude feels earned. As for regret, I think there's a flicker of it, but he'd never admit it aloud, so it comes out as "more than I deserve" instead.
